headline: Draft Bodyworks Ordinance presented by Inspectional Services staff, to license practitioners and establishments citywide
summary: The draft would license practitioners and establishments, require CORI and SORI background checks, and allow at least two unannounced inspections a year for each establishment. Existing legal businesses could stay where they are, while new ones would need properly zoned locations, and all establishments would have 30 days to comply once the rules are enacted. Staff hope to take the draft to public comment in January, with a vote on final rules in February and enactment in March. The presentation estimated between 25 and 30 illicit places operate at any one time, out of approximately 50 to 75 bodyworks places citywide.
discussion: Bodyworks ordinance: Staff said the draft borrows from ordinances in Oxford and Framingham and is still under review by the law department. Questions covered how existing businesses would be treated and whether the number of establishments should be capped, and staff said no cap has been discussed until the number of places is known.

Human trafficking response: Staff said a defined protocol is still being built with inspectors and the police department for people found during inspections. Staff said they are also working with community partners.

Communicable diseases and vaccines: Staff are awaiting a site visit to become a pediatric provider and will bring flu and COVID vaccines to the Veterans Day Parade this Wednesday. Vaccine hesitancy and a church-based outreach network were raised as topics for future conversations.

Winter gun buyback: The program is set for Saturday, December 12th, from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. at the Worcester Police Station, where firearms can be turned in anonymously and gift card values depend on the weapon type.
Next meeting agenda: The next meeting is set for December 14th, with a community health assessment presentation, a winter homelessness update, and a vice chair election proposed.
